newsitem.title: USA: DMX gets merger offer from TCI.
newsitem.headline: DMX gets merger offer from TCI.

text.p: DMX Inc said on Tuesday that Tele-Communications Inc, which owns approximately 45 percent of DMX's outstanding stock, proposed a deal to be acquired by a Tele-Communications Inc venture.
Tele-Communications has proposed forming a new company that would give DMX shareholders class A shares representing 19 percent of the new company, DMX said.

The class A stock would be identical to the class B stock to be held by Tele-Communications except that each class B share would have 10 votes on all matters, while class A shares would have one vote, DMX said.
DMX said Tele-Communications Inc would contribute all of the agreements which it and its controlled affiliates have with residential and commercial DMX subscribers to the new company.

Tele-Communications Inc also set conditions that it would be required to buy the class A shares of the new company for $2 a share, if it did not trade at or above $2 a share for at least 20 consecutive days during the first year of the merger. Tele-Communications Inc would choose whether or not the payment would be either in cash or Tele-Communications Inc shares, DMX said.
Tele-Communications Inc is also proposing to lend DMX $3.5 million at 12.5 percent interest to fund DMX's purchase of tuners for residential and commercial customers of DMX, the company said.
In return, Tele-Communications is seeking the right to distribute DMX's services, DMX said.
DMX said its board of directors appointed a special committee of directors to evaluate the proposal and retain an investment banking firm.
DMX is postponing its annual stockholders meeting from its September 30, 1996 date to a later undisclosed time, it said.
